chunks: "That I should perform salat (prayer) after the time has passed is more beloved to me than that I should perform salat (prayer) while I am in doubt about the time and before the time."

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: more beloved or preferable to me
key_terms.قَبْلَ الْوَقْتِ: before the prescribed time has entered

ai.seo_question: Is it better to delay salat (prayer) than to perform it while uncertain that its time has entered?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes caution in observing the prescribed times of salat (prayer). It teaches that praying after the time out of certainty is preferable to praying before its proper time or while uncertain whether the time has entered.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.671 - Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), said:
"It is more beloved to me to pray after the time (for prayer) has passed than to pray while I am in doubt about whether it is the correct time or before the time (for prayer) has entered."
